champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
ordered_diagnoses: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s presented with a 1-year history of a pruritic, dark red plaque on his right upper eyelid
No remarkable medical history was noted
A 4 × 2-cm erythematous, violaceous, indurated, scaly plaque with some papules on his right upper eyelid
Routine blood tests and biochemistry analysis were within normal limits
perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates around cystically dilated follicular infundibula
Exocytosis of atypical lymphocytes into the epithelium
Admixed plasma cells, eosinophils, and multinucleate giant cells
Alcian blue staining showed focal mild follicular mucin deposition
Lymphocytic infiltrates positive for CD3, CD4, CD5, and CD7
Negative for CD8, CD20, CD30, CD79a, and CD56
CD4 to CD8 cells ratio within hair follicles > 7:1
Monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement was demonstrated

concepts.why: The presence of perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrates, atypical lymphocytes, and a high CD4 to CD8 ratio, along with monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement, are characteristic of Mycosis fungoides.
The presence of lymphocytic infiltrates, atypical lymphocytes, and monoclonal T-cell gene rearrangement suggests a cutaneous lymphoma.
The presence of a pruritic plaque, lymphocytic infiltrates, and admixed plasma cells and eosinophils are consistent with lymphomatoid papulosis.
The presence of a pruritic plaque, lymphocytic infiltrates, and admixed plasma cells and eosinophils could also suggest a pseudolymphoma.
The presence of a pruritic plaque, lymphocytic infiltrates, and admixed plasma cells and eosinophils could also suggest a cutaneous T-cell pseudolymphoma.
